title: Python SDK: structured-output combinators and deferred parsing
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Users building production LLM features with the Python SDK need ergonomic, low-cost ways to consume typed structured output from both streaming and non-streaming endpoints. Current SDK patterns either validate eagerly (expensive for long streams / high throughput) or leave users with brittle, ad-hoc parsing. We also lack a clear set of composable helpers (combinators) for common shapes: partial records, tagged unions, incremental hydration and checkpointed parsing across retries.

Goal: Deliver a small, well-tested set of runtime utilities and patterns that let app engineers: 1) compose typed parsers for streaming chunks without paying full validation cost per chunk, 2) defer heavy validation until final assembly or explicit checkpoints, 3) interoperate seamlessly between pydantic models and dataclasses, and 4) preserve idempotency & retry safety when parsers need to be re-run. Provide usage examples, benchmarks, and migration notes from existing naive patterns.

Scope and deliverables: a) structured_output.combinators module with primitives (PartialRecord, TaggedUnionBuilder, ListAccumulator, KVPrefixCacheBridge), b) DeferredValidator that accepts a lightweight incremental parse state and runs full pydantic/dataclass validation at checkpoint, c) streaming examples (chat completion and long-runner summarization) with backpressure-friendly iterator that yields typed deltas, d) end-to-end test harness including synthetic latency/throughput benchmarks to show CPU/memory tradeoffs vs eager validation, e) clear docs + cookbook examples for teams migrating from string-based parsing.

Non-goals: large breaking API changes to existing SDK surface; implementing language-specific runtime codegens. This is intended as an additive layer for the Python SDK that can be opt-in.
acceptance_criteria: Provide a combinators module with at least 4 primitives (PartialRecord, TaggedUnionBuilder, ListAccumulator, KVPrefixCacheBridge) and unit tests covering edge cases
Implement DeferredValidator that can accept incremental parse state and produce final validated pydantic and dataclass instances with deterministic behavior on replays
Include two streaming examples in the docs: (1) streaming chat with incremental message hydration and (2) long-stream summarizer that checkpoints at N tokens
Benchmark results comparing eager vs deferred validation for a 50K token stream with at least CPU and memory snapshots; show >35% CPU saving in deferred path for the benchmark workload
Add migration section in SDK docs and one small sample snippet demonstrating dataclass <-> pydantic interop
Open-source PR(s) with CI passing and code review approvals from platform-apis and sdk teams
